engine_note: The archival prior below was produced by an EARLIER engine, before the L8 default-seed DSBPL restart, the L9 widened Ep caps / BOUND_CAPPED diagnosis, and the L28 residual-coherence acquittal. bb_union_rule.definition: a block counts as BB-significant if (LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 AND BANDBB_KT > 1.05 keV) OR (LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 AND CPLBB_KT > 1.05 keV) - BOTH nested tests, union
bb_union_rule.class: CPL-side-only, high-kT shoulder in the time-integrated block; NOT the L28 edge-constrained (<~5 keV) class, and NOT a Band-side detection anywhere
bb_union_rule.T8_baseline_discipline: the two nested margins disagree by 4.1 in the SAME block (Band baseline 5.64 vs CPL baseline 9.77). Any BB verdict for this burst MUST name its baseline - this is the published twin of Wang+2019's Band-vs-CPL baseline split.

cpl.note: xc is an E-FOLDING energy; Ep = (2+index)*xc = 224 keV

time_integrated_blk_minus1.aic_winner_margin: Band+BB beats SBPL by only 0.69 AIC and Band by 1.64 - far below the project's dAIC>=10 framework threshold. The 'winner' here is a coin-flip among Band/SBPL/Band+BB.
time_integrated_blk_minus1.dsbpl_flag: DSBPL has the LOWEST AIC of all six (7746.155, i.e. 10.8 below Band+BB) and LRT_DSBPL_SBPL = 14.81 >= 9.2, but DSBPL_VALID = False, so it was excluded from the winner selection. Its parameters: alpha1 = +2.500, xb = 11.82 keV, alpha2 = -1.154, xp = 190.74 keV, beta = -2.444. alpha1 = +2.5 with a break at 11.8 keV places the first segment essentially below the NaI threshold - the classic unconstrained-low-break failure mode that the validity gate is there to catch. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST IMPORTANT ITEM TO RE-EXAMINE with the current engine.

dsbpl_summary.class: no VALID two-break block; the only block clearing the LRT threshold is the time-integrated one and it fails validity

gbm_catalog.dets: n9,na,nb,b1 (scat_detector_mask 00000000011101) - IDENTICAL to our stamped detector set

external_prior.morphology_dispute: four contemporaneous circulars (GCN 12859, 12872, 12874, 12884) call the light curve multi-peaked (three overlapping peaks); two refereed samples classify it single-pulse (Shao+2017/Jiang+2021 'bright single-pulse'; Moss+2022 'Simple-pulse'/'Symmetric-like'). UNRESOLVED.
external_prior.no_prior_spectral_component_claim: NO paper in the 41-paper harvest claims a blackbody, a low-energy break, or a two-break spectrum for this burst. The only physical prompt model applied to it is Jiang+2021's photospheric lag interpretation, which rests on a lag with ~5x uncertainty. The two-break question is UNCONSTRAINED by prior literature here - the good case for a blind test.

predictions: P-A1 (BB, Band side - falsifiable): NO block will pass LRT_BANDBB_BAND >= 9.2 AND BANDBB_KT > 1.05 keV. Archival max = 5.644 at blk-1; the highest time-resolved value is 4.635 at blk9. FALSIFIED if any block reaches 9.2 on the Band baseline.

P-A2 (BB, CPL side - falsifiable): LRT_CPLBB_CPL >= 9.2 will recur in the time-integrated block (archival 9.773) and in AT MOST one time-resolved block; the runner-up blk0 sits at 8.010, so a second passing block would be a new result. The CPL+BB kT will land in the 15-30 keV range (archival 21.26 +/- 3.46 keV at blk-1, 17.94 at blk0) - the HIGH-kT shoulder class, NOT the L28 edge-constrained (<~5 keV) class. FALSIFIED if the recovered kT is <5 keV or if >=3 blocks pass.

P-A3 (two-break - the burst's live question): the time-integrated block WILL again show LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2 (archival 14.812) and DSBPL will again have the lowest raw AIC (archival 7746.155, 10.8 below the next model), but the fit will AGAIN be flagged invalid - the low break railing to the bottom of the NaI band (archival xb = 11.82 keV with alpha1 = +2.500). PREDICTION: with the L8 restart and L9 widened caps, either (a) the DSBPL restart finds a physical solution with xb in 20-80 keV and alpha1 in [-1.2, -0.5], in which case bn120119170 ENTERS the two-break census, or (b) it re-rails and is diagnosed BOUND_CAPPED / OUT_OF_FAMILY. I predict (b) at ~65% - the archival alpha1 = +2.5 is a rising segment, which is not a soft break but an unconstrained tail. FALSIFIED either way by the recorded diagnosis; a silent 'DSBPL_VALID=False' with no diagnosis code is a pipeline failure, not an outcome.
P-A4 (no time-resolved two-break): no time-resolved block (blk0..blk9) will reach LRT_DSBPL_SBPL >= 9.2. Archival max over blk0..9 = 5.777 (blk9). FALSIFIED if any resolved block clears 9.2.

P-B1 (catalog anchor, hard numbers): the time-integrated Band fit over [-1, +47] s will give alpha = -0.90 +/- 0.08, Ep = 180 +/- 20 keV, beta in [-2.45, -2.15]. Anchors: GBM catalog flnc_band over [-2.048, +57.344] s (alpha = -0.955 +/- 0.032, Ep = 182.76 +/- 10.45, beta = -2.366 +/- 0.160) and archival blk-1 (alpha = -0.882 +/- 0.057, Ep = 178.19 +/- 15.64, beta = -2.280 +/- 0.138). Note our window is 10.3 s SHORTER at the tail end, which should push Ep slightly HARDER (the late blocks are the softest: blk9 Ep = 63 keV).

P-B2 (SBPL break energy): the time-integrated SBPL break will land at 120-135 keV. Anchors: GBM catalog flnc_sbpl brken = 123.68 +/- 9.11 keV (brksc fixed 0.30) and archival blk-1 SBPL_EBREAK = 125.64 keV. These two independent pipelines agree to 1.6%, which makes this the tightest external check available for this burst.

P-B3 (winner family): the time-integrated AIC winner will be one of {SBPL, Band, Band+BB} with a margin BELOW the project's dAIC >= 10 threshold - i.e. the honest verdict is 'no winner'. Archival spread across those three is 1.64 AIC. FALSIFIED if any single-component model wins by >= 10.

P-B4 (spectral evolution): Ep(Band) will fall monotonically over the last four blocks. Archival: blk6 202.9 -> blk7 121.6 -> blk8 109.5 -> blk9 63.3 keV, i.e. a clean soft-tail decay; alpha stays near -0.85 through blk8 and hardens to -0.19 in blk9 where Ep drops below 70 keV (an alpha-Ep anticorrelation that is usually a fit degeneracy, not physics - flag it, do not report it).

P-B5 (temporal, Step 7): T90 will reproduce 55.3 +/- 6.2 s (50-300 keV) ONLY if the fit window is extended; our stamped window ends at +47 s while the catalog T90 ends at +58.4 s, so any T90 measured inside our window is a LOWER LIMIT and must be reported as such. MVT will land at or below 0.463 s (Golkhou+2015 upper limit) and plausibly near 0.20 s (their Figure 3).

P-C (identity / coverage, non-spectral but falsifiable): the burst has a ~100 s dim tail (Moss+2022 Sec 5.2) that our window excludes entirely. PREDICTION: extending the source window to +85 s (Golkhou's T100 stop) would add >= 2 additional Bayesian blocks with Ep < 70 keV and would NOT change the two-break verdict of the bright complex. Testable whenever a window-sensitivity run is done; it is NOT an argument for changing the approved window.
known_risks_to_this_freeze: The archival prior predates the L8/L9 engine fixes; its BB and two-break counts are lower limits. P-A1/P-A2/P-A4 are therefore predictions that the new engine will find MORE, not less - if they hold exactly, that is weak evidence the fixes did not bite on this burst.

LLE/LAT data are absent from data/bn120119170/ although the burst was 31.4 deg off the LAT boresight (GCN 12874). Every prediction above is GBM-only. If the LAT/LLE arm is later acquired, the high-energy predictions (beta, DSBPL upper segment) must be re-frozen - a joint fit is a different experiment.

The fermigbrst row carries dec = -9.803 while the true (XRT) position is -9.08177. Our responses were generated from whichever position the pipeline used; Ahlgren+2020 measured the effect of exactly this substitution on exactly this burst and found <1 sigma, so it is bounded but not zero.
